findings.title: totalPages overcounts by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages is computed as floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages, and with 100 members it reports 3, but only 2 pages of data exist. The extra page is empty: the server returns no rows for offset 50 when total is 50. The next action clamps offset to user_count rather than to the start of the last page, so from page 1 of a 50-member group, Next moves to offset 50 and shows an empty '2/2' page. Every group whose size is a multiple of the page size gets a phantom empty last page. The fix is ceil(user_count / limit) or the equivalent.

findings.title: Remove link is shown for members of automatic groups
findings.body: The '{{#unless automatic}}' guard is evaluated against the item being rendered (a Discourse.User inside the {{each}} item view), not against the admin group controller where 'automatic' is defined. The property is therefore undefined and the remove '×' link is rendered for every member, including automatic groups where removal is forbidden. Clicking it runs the confirm dialog, then the server returns 422 (can_not_modify_automatic in add/remove_member). The removeMember promise in group.js has no error handler, so the admin gets no feedback. The flag needs to be read from the controller explicitly, or the control hidden from group.hbs.

findings.title: Public members list silently truncated to 50 with no pagination controls
findings.body: The public members route now calls findMembers() with the default limit of 50 (groups_controller.rb defaults limit to 50 for every group, not only automatic ones). This template has no next/previous controls, so for any group with more than 50 members the members beyond the first 50 cannot be seen. Before this change, non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned up to 200. This is a functional regression for larger groups. Either add pagination to this page or request the full list here.

findings.title: members endpoint response changed from an array to an object, breaking existing clients
findings.body: GET /groups/:name/members.json previously returned a bare JSON array. It now returns {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}. This is a public endpoint, so any existing API client or script that iterates the top-level array will break. The default page size of 50 also silently truncates results for clients that previously received every member of a non-automatic group. Nothing in this PR versions the endpoint or documents the change.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level even though the form lets the admin set it
findings.body: The rewritten create action sets name and visible but never reads params[:alias_level]. The admin group form shows the alias_level combo-box for new groups too (it is not inside {{#if id}}), and asJSON sends alias_level. An admin who picks a value for a new group has it silently discarded and the group is saved with the default. The update action handles this with 'group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?', and create should do the same. No spec covers it.

findings.title: Changed members endpoint contract has no test coverage in this PR
findings.body: The members action's response shape, default limit, limit/offset handling and total count were all changed, and automatic groups now paginate like others. No spec change in this PR covers any of this (the groups controller spec is not touched). Tests should assert the {members, meta} shape, that total reflects the full membership, and that limit/offset select the right page for both automatic and non-automatic groups.

findings.title: Offset clamp uses the stale user_count, leaving an empty page after removing the last member
findings.body: findMembers clamps offset to the user_count from before the request. Take a group with 51 members on page 2 (offset 50) and remove the one member on that page. removeMember then calls findMembers, which clamps to the old user_count of 51 and keeps offset 50. The server returns an empty page with total 50, so the admin sees an empty page and a page counter past the last page. The clamp should use the new total from the response or the server should clamp.

findings.title: Negative limit or offset query params cause a 500 from Postgres
findings.body: limit and offset come straight from params with to_i and go into .limit() and .offset(). A request with offset=-1 produces a negative OFFSET, which Postgres rejects with an error, so the request fails with a 500. This path now runs for every group rather than only automatic ones. limit has no upper bound either. Both should be validated, for example limit clamped to 1..N and offset to >= 0.

findings.title: Pressing Enter in the name field triggers the Add members button instead of Save
findings.body: The new <form> wrapper has no submit handler. The Add members <button> has no type attribute, so it is a submit button and is the first submit button in the form. Browsers implicitly submit a form on Enter using its first submit button, so Enter in the Name field of an existing group clicks Add (addMembers) rather than Save. The name change is not saved. Giving the Add button type='button' would make Save the default button again.

findings.title: CSS rule targets an element id that no longer exists
findings.body: The rule input#group-users is still in the stylesheet, but group.hbs now renders the user selector with id='user-selector', so this 600px width rule never applies. The selector falls back to the 350px rule added in this PR. Update the selector or remove the dead rule.

findings.title: Renaming a non-automatic group via update is no longer tested
findings.body: The removed 'is able to update group members' test was the only spec that renamed a non-automatic group through update and checked that name and membership persisted. The new .update context only covers the automatic-group no-op. The non-automatic rename path (group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic), alias_level updates and visible updates now have no coverage.
